mainTopic: How long בין השמשות lasts and how to judge it, the wicker-basket size dispute, and how the twilight opinions apply to כהנים' immersion and to שבת versus תרומה
overview: This amud finishes the מחלוקת between רבה and רב יוסף about how long בין השמשות lasts: three-quarters of a מיל versus two-thirds, a gap of one-twelfth of a מיל. With a large wicker basket (חַלְּתָא), the two argue the other way around. There רב יוסף allows the bigger size, and אביי reports that in a real case רבה forbade even two כור, following a משנה that treats such huge containers as non-vessels. A story about אביי and רבא teaches that to judge twilight you watch the western sky, the side that makes the east turn red. רבי חנינא gives a way to feel רבי נחמיה's half-מיל measure at הר הכרמל, which leads to a side-teaching about בארה של מרים and a moving spring. שמואל then rules that כהנים may immerse during רבי יהודה's twilight, and the גמרא explains that this follows רבי יוסי, whose short twilight comes only after רבי יהודה's ends. Finally, רבי יוחנן rules like רבי יהודה for שבת and like רבי יוסי for תרומה. The גמרא challenges the תרומה half: if it is about immersion, that time is still a doubt. The answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רב יוסף: twilight lasts two-thirds of a מיל
steps.stepSummary: This amud opens with the end of רב יוסף's view: בין השמשות lasts as long as it takes to walk two-thirds of a מיל.
steps.simpleTranslation: [רב יוסף said: בין השמשות lasts the time it takes to walk] two-thirds of a מיל.
steps.whatsHappening: We are joining the end of a statement. רבה said בין השמשות lasts the time to walk three-quarters of a מיל, and here רב יוסף says two-thirds of a מיל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Twilight is measured by walking time, not by a clock. רב יוסף's measure (2/3) is a little shorter than רבה's (3/4). The next steps work out exactly how big that difference is.

keyTerms.meaning: a mil, a distance of 2,000 אמות, used here as a measure of walking time
twilight, the in-between period after sunset

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a new statement. It is the tail end of רב יוסף's opinion from the end of the previous daf, which is answering רבה's 'three-quarters of a מיל.'

phrases.english: two-thirds of a mil.
phrases.notes: End of רב יוסף's view. רבה had said three-quarters of a מיל.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the רבה / רב יוסף dispute begun on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רב יוסף, בין השמשות lasts the time it takes to walk two-thirds of a מיל.

steps.title: What is the actual difference between them?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how big the gap really is between three-quarters and two-thirds of a מיל.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question to set up the next line: in practice, how far apart are these two opinions?
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not an attack on either view. It is a request to measure the gap between 3/4 and 2/3 precisely.

phrases.english: What is between them?
phrases.notes: Asking for the practical size of the gap.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the size of the gap between רבה and רב יוסף.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact size of the difference between 3/4 of a מיל and 2/3 of a מיל.

steps.title: The gap is half of a sixth
steps.stepSummary: The difference is half a דַּנְקָא (a sixth), which equals one-twelfth of a מיל.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference between them is half of a sixth (one-twelfth of a מיל).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: the two opinions differ by only one-twelfth of a מיל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The math is 3/4 = 9/12 and 2/3 = 8/12, so the gap is 1/12. A דַּנְקָא is one-sixth, so half a דַּנְקָא is one-twelfth. רבה's twilight is the longer of the two.

keyTerms.meaning: there is between them (the difference is)

phrases.english: There is between them half of a sixth.
phrases.notes: Three-quarters is 9/12 and two-thirds is 8/12, so the gap is 1/12 of a מיל.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The difference is one-twelfth of a מיל. רבה's measure is the longer one.

steps.title: With the wicker basket, their positions are reversed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that in the case of a large wicker basket, רבה and רב יוסף argue in the opposite direction.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the reverse is true regarding a wicker basket.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא tells us that in another case, a basket, these same two אמוראים swap which of them gives the larger number, and the next steps show it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With twilight, רבה's number (3/4) was bigger than רב יוסף's. With the basket, רב יוסף will allow the bigger size. The word 'reverse' refers only to which one gives the bigger measurement.

phrases.english: And its reverse is with a wicker basket.
phrases.notes: In this case רב יוסף gives the larger measure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares the twilight dispute to a second dispute between the same אמוראים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the basket case, רבה and רב יוסף argue in the opposite direction from the twilight case.

steps.title: רבה: a basket of two כור may be moved, but not three
steps.stepSummary: רבה rules that a basket holding two כור may be moved on שבת, but one holding three כור may not.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבה said: a wicker basket that holds two כור may be moved on שבת. One that holds three כור may not be moved.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רבה's ruling on how big a basket can be and still count as a movable vessel on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only a כלי may be moved on שבת. Once a basket gets too huge, it stops counting as a כלי and is treated like a fixed structure. רבה draws the line between two and three כור.

keyTerms.meaning: a large dry measure, equal to 30 סאה

phrases.english: As Rabba said:

phrases.aramaic: חַלְּתָא בַּת תְּרֵי כוֹרֵי — שְׁרֵי לְטַלְטוֹלַהּ,
phrases.english: a wicker basket of two kor — it is permitted to move it,
and one of three kor — it is forbidden to move it.
phrases.notes: At that size it is too large to count as a כלי.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins showing the reversal announced in step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבה: two כור may be moved, three כור may not.

steps.title: רב יוסף: even three כור may be moved, but not four
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף permits moving a three-כור basket and forbids only a four-כור basket.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: a basket of three כור may also be moved. One of four כור is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רב יוסף's opposing view, which allows a larger basket than רבה does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here רב יוסף has the bigger number (four כור), while רבה has the smaller one (three כור). That is the 'reverse' of the twilight case, where רבה had the bigger number.

phrases.english: And Rav Yosef said:
one of three kor is also permitted,
one of four kor is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view, which completes the reversal.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רב יוסף: three כור may be moved, four כור may not.
steps.whatToRemember: Twilight: רבה says 3/4 מיל and רב יוסף says 2/3, so רבה is larger. Basket: רבה forbids three כור and רב יוסף forbids only four, so רב יוסף is larger.

steps.title: אביי: in a real case, רבה forbade even two כור
steps.stepSummary: אביי reports that when he asked רבה in an actual situation, רבה did not even allow a two-כור basket.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: I asked my master (רבה) when the case actually came up, and he did not permit me even a basket of two כור.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי tells us that רבה's practical ruling was stricter than the view quoted in his name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In theory, רבה permits two כור. But when a real case came up, he was stricter and forbade it. This sets up the question of what source רבה was relying on.

keyTerms.meaning: at the time of an actual case

phrases.english: Abaye said:
I asked the Master at the time of an actual case,

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲפִילּוּ בַּת תְּרֵי כוֹרֵי לָא שְׁרָא לִי.
phrases.english: and he did not permit me even one of two kor.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: בְּעַי מִינֵּיהּ דְּמָר בִּשְׁעַת מַעֲשֶׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a stricter practical ruling from רבה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In practice, רבה forbade moving even a two-כור basket.
steps.whyThisMatters: A ruling given in an actual case (מעשה) carries special weight, so this report matters for how the halacha is decided.

steps.title: Whose view was רבה following?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which earlier opinion רבה's strict practical ruling is based on.
steps.simpleTranslation: In accordance with whom?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source behind רבה's strict ruling. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Forbidding even two כור needs some basis. The גמרא looks for a תנא who would treat a two-כור container as not a real כלי.

phrases.english: According to whom?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the ruling in step 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא's opinion supports forbidding a two-כור basket.

steps.title: Like the משנה: huge containers are not vessels
steps.stepSummary: רבה follows a משנה which rules that very large containers holding two כור of dry goods are טהורים, meaning they do not count as כלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Like this תנא, as we learned: a straw beehive-shaped barrel, a reed barrel, and the water cistern of an Alexandrian ship are טהורים, even though they have bottoms and hold forty סאה of liquid, which is two כור of dry goods.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבה relied on a משנה from the laws of טומאה, which says such large containers are not considered vessels.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Something too big to count as a כלי cannot become טמא. These containers hold two כור, and the משנה says they stay טהור. So by this view, two כור is already 'not a vessel,' and that is why רבה would not allow moving it on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: the water tank of an Alexandrian ship
a bottom (so it can hold things)
a measure of volume; 30 סאה equal one כור

steps.confusionAlert: 'טהורים' here does not mean the containers were purified. It means they are too large to be considered a כלי at all, so they cannot receive טומאה.

phrases.english: Like this tanna, as we learned:
a straw barrel and a reed barrel
and the cistern of an Alexandrian ship,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהֶם שׁוּלַיִם
phrases.english: even though they have bottoms
and they hold forty se'ah of liquid
which is two kor of dry goods —
they are pure.
phrases.notes: They are too large to be considered vessels.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 8 by naming the source.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבה follows the משנה that treats two-כור containers as non-vessels, so they may not be moved on שבת.

steps.title: אביי: the heap above the rim is one-third
steps.stepSummary: From the משנה's numbers, אביי learns that the heap of dry goods piled above the rim makes up one-third of the total.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: learn from this that the heap (the extra amount dry goods add above the rim) is one-third.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי makes a side calculation from the משנה: a vessel holds more when filled with dry goods than with liquid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Forty סאה of liquid equals two כור (sixty סאה) of dry goods. Dry goods can be heaped up above the rim, while liquid cannot. The extra twenty סאה is one-third of the sixty.

keyTerms.meaning: the heap of dry goods piled above the rim

phrases.english: Abaye said: learn from it
that this heap is one-third.
phrases.notes: 20 of 60 סאה is the heaped part.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a side inference from the משנה quoted in step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Dry goods heaped above the rim add one-third to the total (60 סאה dry versus 40 סאה liquid).

steps.title: אביי asks רבא why he looks west
steps.stepSummary: אביי sees רבא looking west to judge twilight and challenges him from a ברייתא that speaks of the eastern sky turning red.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי saw רבא gazing toward the west. He said to him: but wasn't it taught that twilight lasts as long as the face of the east is red?
steps.whatsHappening: A story begins. אביי challenges רבא's practice of looking west by quoting a ברייתא that seems to point east.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא defines בין השמשות as lasting 'as long as the face of the east is red.' Read simply, that means you should look at the eastern sky. So why was רבא looking west?

keyTerms.meaning: but wasn't it taught (in a ברייתא)?

phrases.english: Abaye saw Rava
gazing toward the west.
He said to him: But wasn't it taught
'as long as the face of the east is red'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the topic of twilight through a story.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's practice of looking west to judge בין השמשות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא mentions the eastern sky, which suggests you should look east, not west.

steps.title: It means the sky that makes the east red
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that 'פני מזרח' means the western sky, which causes the east to turn red.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: do you think it means the actual face of the east? No. It means the face that makes the east red.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers by re-reading the ברייתא's words: the point is the western sky, which reddens the east.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase is read as 'the face that reddens the east.' After sunset, the remaining light in the west casts a red glow eastward. So the place to check is the west.

phrases.english: He said to him: Do you think
the actual face of the east?
No, the face that reddens the east.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the wording of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'פני מזרח' means the eastern sky itself.
steps.terutzMaskana: It means the western sky, which causes the east to turn red.

steps.title: Another version: רבא corrects אביי
steps.stepSummary: In a second version, רבא sees אביי looking east and teaches him that the ברייתא means the western sky.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: רבא saw אביי gazing east. He said to him: do you think it means the actual face of the east? It means the face that makes the east red.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different version of the same story, with the roles of the two אמוראים switched.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only the story details change: here אביי looked east and רבא corrected him. The halachic point is the same in both versions: look west.

phrases.english: Some say:
Rava saw Abaye
gazing toward the east.
He said to him: Do you think
the actual face of the east?
The face that reddens the east.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Retells the story of steps 11 and 12 with the roles reversed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Whoever said it, the ברייתא means the western sky.

steps.title: Mnemonic: a window
steps.stepSummary: The memory aid is a window: the light coming in through it shows up on the opposite wall.
steps.simpleTranslation: And your mnemonic is: a window.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the story with a memory aid for remembering to look west.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When sunlight comes through a window, its glow appears on the wall across from it. In the same way, the west 'shines' its red onto the east, so the west is the source to watch.
steps.whatToRemember: To judge בין השמשות, check the western sky. 'פני מזרח' means the sky that makes the east red, like light through a window lighting the opposite wall.

phrases.english: And your mnemonic: a window.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a memory aid for the conclusion of steps 12 and 13.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The western sky, which reddens the east, is what determines בין השמשות.

steps.title: רבי נחמיה's measure of twilight
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי נחמיה's view from the ברייתא: בין השמשות lasts as long as it takes to walk half a מיל after sunset.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי נחמיה says: twilight lasts as long as it takes a person to walk half a מיל after the sun sets.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes another opinion from the ברייתא about how long בין השמשות lasts. This is a setup line: the next step explains how to picture this measure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, רבי יהודה described twilight by how the sky looks after sunset, as the redness fades and the sky darkens. It was רבה and רב יוסף who later turned his twilight into walking time (three-quarters or two-thirds of a מיל). רבי נחמיה gives his own measure directly in walking time: half a מיל, which is shorter.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who gives his own measure for the length of twilight
Half a מיל, the time it takes to walk about half a Talmudic mile

phrases.english: Rabbi Nechemya says:
The time it takes for a person to walk
half a mil, from when the sun sets.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the ברייתא's list of twilight measures, after the side discussion about which direction to look
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי נחמיה, בין השמשות lasts the time it takes to walk half a מיל after sunset.

steps.title: A practical way to feel רבי נחמיה's measure
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא says: when the sun is leaving the top of הר הכרמל, go down, immerse in the sea, and come up. That stretch of time is רבי נחמיה's measure.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא said: Whoever wants to know רבי נחמיה's measure should notice when the sun is left only on the top of הר הכרמל. Then he should go down, immerse in the sea, and come back up. That amount of time is רבי נחמיה's measure.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנינא turns רבי נחמיה's measure into a real-life experience. He uses the sunlight on top of the כרמל and a dip in the nearby sea.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone standing at the shore sees the sun set, but the top of the כרמל is still lit. The time it takes to go down, immerse, and climb back up equals half a מיל of walking. This gives a physical picture of the measure.

keyTerms.meaning: The אמורא who gives the practical demonstration
His measure, meaning the set amount of time
The top of הר הכרמל, the mountain next to the sea

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina said:

phrases.aramaic: הָרוֹצֶה לֵידַע שִׁיעוּרוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי נְחֶמְיָה
phrases.english: One who wants to know Rabbi Nechemya's measure
should leave the sun on the top of the Carmel
phrases.notes: Meaning: start when the sun's light is left only on the mountaintop

phrases.english: and go down, immerse in the sea, and come up
and that is Rabbi Nechemya's measure.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָרוֹצֶה לֵידַע שִׁיעוּרוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי נְחֶמְיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a concrete illustration of the measure stated in Step 15
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Going down from the כרמל, immersing in the sea, and coming back up equals רבי נחמיה's twilight period.

steps.title: Seeing בארה של מרים from הר הכרמל
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא says that from the top of the כרמל you can see a sieve-like rock in the sea, and that is בארה של מרים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא said: Whoever wants to see בארה של מרים should climb to the top of the כרמל and look out. He will see something like a sieve in the sea, and that is בארה של מרים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a related teaching because it also begins with 'whoever wants to…' and also involves the כרמל and the sea. This is a side-topic, not part of the twilight discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בארה של מרים is the well that gave water to בני ישראל in the מדבר. רבי חייא says its resting place can be seen from the כרמל as a sieve-shaped rock in the sea.

keyTerms.meaning: Miriam's well, which traveled with בני ישראל in the מדבר
And he should look out from a high place

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new step in the twilight debate. The גמרא links it only because of the shared wording and setting. The twilight topic returns in Step 19.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiya said:
One who wants to see Miriam's well
should climb to the top of the Carmel and look out
and he will see something like a sieve in the sea
and that is Miriam's well.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Associative side-trip, triggered by the same opening phrase and the same location as Step 16
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The sieve-like rock seen in the sea from the כרמל is בארה של מרים.

steps.title: A moving spring is pure
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that a spring that moves from place to place is טהור and counts as a real spring. Such a spring is בארה של מרים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: A spring that moves around is טהור, and that is בארה של מרים.
steps.whatsHappening: Still on the topic of בארה של מרים, רב adds a halachic point. A spring that moves still counts as a real spring.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might think a spring has to be fixed in the ground to count as a מעיין, and that moving water is like drawn water. רב rules that a moving spring is still a kosher spring. His example is בארה של מרים, which traveled with בני ישראל.

keyTerms.meaning: A natural spring, which purifies even with flowing water
That moves from place to place
Pure; here, valid as a spring for purification

steps.whatToRemember: The side-topic ends with a ruling: a spring keeps its status as a spring even if it moves, and בארה של מרים is the example.

phrases.english: Rav said:
A spring that moves is pure
and that is Miriam's well.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a halachic ruling connected to בארה של מרים from Step 17
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A moving spring is טהור and counts as a real spring, like בארה של מרים.

steps.title: Priests may immerse during רבי יהודה's twilight
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of שמואל says that כהנים may immerse during רבי יהודה's בין השמשות and still count it as daytime immersion.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: During רבי יהודה's twilight, כהנים may immerse.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the twilight topic with a new ruling from שמואל. It is about a טמא כהן who immerses so that sunset will come afterward and he may eat תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כהן who immerses may eat תרומה only after the sun sets on his immersion (הערב שמש). שמואל says that an immersion during רבי יהודה's twilight period still counts as before nightfall. That is surprising, and it sets up the next question about whose view this follows.

keyTerms.meaning: Twilight, the in-between period after sunset
Priests immerse in a מקוה to become pure
רב יהודה reporting a teaching of his teacher שמואל

steps.whyThisMatters: This connects the abstract twilight debate to a practical question: when a כהן's immersion still counts as daytime, so that he may eat תרומה that night.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
During the twilight of Rabbi Yehuda,
priests may immerse in it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the twilight discussion after the side-trip about בארה של מרים
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An immersion during the period of רבי יהודה's twilight still counts as daytime immersion for כהנים.

steps.title: Whose view is this? Not רבי יהודה's own
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whose view שמואל's ruling follows. It cannot be רבי יהודה himself, because for him twilight is a doubt.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to whom? If you say according to רבי יהודה, that time is a doubt for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which תנא's view שמואל's ruling follows. It quickly rules out the obvious answer, רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, his twilight period might be day and might be night. A כהן immersing then cannot be sure the sun has not already set on him. So the ruling cannot fit רבי יהודה's own view.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (introducing a suggestion the גמרא will reject)
A doubt; unclear whether it is day or night

steps.confusionAlert: 'בין השמשות דרבי יהודה' names a stretch of time, not necessarily the person whose ruling is being followed. The גמרא is about to separate the two.

phrases.english: According to whom?
If you say according to Rabbi Yehuda
it is a doubt for him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the attribution of שמואל's ruling from Step 19
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא's view allows immersion during רבי יהודה's twilight period

steps.title: It follows רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the time period is רבי יהודה's twilight, but the ruling follows רבי יוסי, for whom that time is still day.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, during the period of רבי יהודה's twilight, according to רבי יוסי, כהנים may immerse.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question. The time period is measured by רבי יהודה, but the halacha follows רבי יוסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי's twilight is very short and comes later. So during the time רבי יהודה calls twilight, רבי יוסי still considers it full day. A כהן who immerses then will have sunset come afterward and may eat תרומה.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא whose twilight is a blink of an eye and comes later

phrases.english: Rather, during Rabbi Yehuda's twilight,
according to Rabbi Yosei, priests may immerse in it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, בֵּין הַשְּׁמָשׁוֹת דְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה, לְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 20
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ruling follows רבי יוסי, who considers רבי יהודה's twilight period to still be day.

steps.title: Isn't that obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that this is obvious: if for רבי יוסי it is still day, of course one may immerse.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges שמואל's ruling as unnecessary. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי יוסי's twilight comes after רבי יהודה's, then רבי יהודה's period is daytime for רבי יוסי. Allowing immersion then seems too obvious to need a teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious! (an objection that a teaching adds nothing new)

phrases.english: That is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for the ruling as explained in Step 21
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling as explained according to רבי יוסי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the time is plainly day for רבי יוסי, the ruling teaches nothing new.

steps.title: רבי יהודה's twilight ends before רבי יוסי's begins
steps.stepSummary: The ruling was needed because one might think רבי יוסי's short twilight falls inside the end of רבי יהודה's. It teaches that רבי יהודה's twilight ends first, and only then does רבי יוסי's begin.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said that רבי יוסי's twilight is drawn into and falls within רבי יהודה's twilight. So the teaching tells us that רבי יהודה's twilight finishes, and only then does רבי יוסי's twilight begin.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the 'obvious' objection by showing the ruling teaches something new about the order of the two periods.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We might have thought רבי יוסי's blink-of-an-eye twilight sits at the tail end of רבי יהודה's period. If so, it would already be night by the end of רבי יהודה's period, and immersing then would be too late. שמואל teaches that the periods do not overlap: רבי יוסי's twilight comes only after רבי יהודה's ends, so all of רבי יהודה's period is day for רבי יוסי.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said (introducing a mistaken assumption)
Is drawn into and falls within

steps.whatToRemember: The two twilights are back-to-back, not overlapping: first רבי יהודה's twilight (three-quarters of a מיל according to רבה, two-thirds according to רב יוסף), then רבי יוסי's blink. So a כהן may immerse during all of רבי יהודה's period according to רבי יוסי.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not picture רבי יוסי's twilight as one moment inside רבי יהודה's period. The conclusion is that it comes entirely after it.

phrases.english: You might have said:
Rabbi Yosei's twilight
is drawn into and falls within Rabbi Yehuda's
so he teaches us
that Rabbi Yehuda's twilight ends,

phrases.aramaic: וַהֲדַר מַתְחֵיל בֵּין הַשְּׁמָשׁוֹת דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי.
phrases.english: and only then does Rabbi Yosei's twilight begin.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא objection of Step 22
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the ruling's new point (מהו דתימא / קא משמע לן)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוסי's twilight falls within the end of רבי יהודה's, so by then it would be too late to immerse.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יהודה's twilight ends completely, and only then does רבי יוסי's begin. So all of רבי יהודה's period is day for רבי יוסי.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן splits the ruling between שבת and תרומה
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה quotes רבי יוחנן. The הלכה follows רבי יהודה for שבת and רבי יוסי for תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: For שבת, the הלכה follows רבי יהודה. For תרומה, the הלכה follows רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement comes in. רבי יוחנן rules on the argument between רבי יהודה and רבי יוסי about בין השמשות, and he gives a different answer for each area of law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה's twilight starts earlier, so following him for שבת means we stop work sooner. רבי יוסי's twilight is very short and comes later, so following him for תרומה gives a later cutoff. The ruling is split by topic instead of picking one opinion for everything.

keyTerms.meaning: With regard to, in the matter of
The holy portion given to a כהן, which he may eat only when he is ritually pure
The Sabbath. Here the question is when it begins and ends at twilight.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume one rabbi must win on every topic. רבי יוחנן follows רבי יהודה in one area and רבי יוסי in another.
steps.whyThisMatters: This split ruling is the base of the rest of the sugya. The גמרא will now work out what 'תרומה' here actually refers to.

phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Ḥana said
Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
The halakha follows Rabbi Yehuda with regard to Shabbat,
and the halakha follows Rabbi Yosei with regard to teruma.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new authoritative ruling on the same argument about בין השמשות discussed in steps 19–23.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For שבת, follow רבי יהודה's twilight. For תרומה, follow רבי יוסי's twilight.

steps.title: The שבת ruling makes sense, but what does the תרומה ruling refer to?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts the שבת half as a strict ruling. It asks which case the תרומה half is about.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense to follow רבי יהודה for שבת, because that is the strict choice. But for תרומה, what case is he talking about?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא agrees with the first half of the ruling and asks for clarification of the second half. This sets up the next step, where the גמרא will test a possible answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, twilight is a doubt. Being strict about a doubt in a Torah law like שבת is normal. But 'תרומה' could mean several things, such as when a כהן may immerse or when he may eat. So the גמרא needs to know which case is meant.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted, it makes sense (this part is fine)
What is it? (which case is meant)

phrases.english: Granted, the halakha follows Rabbi Yehuda
with regard to Shabbat, as a stringency.
phrases.notes: His earlier twilight means שבת starts sooner, which is the strict outcome.

phrases.english: But with regard to teruma, what is the case?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה לְעִנְיַן שַׁבָּת לְחוּמְרָא אֲבָל לְעִנְיַן תְּרוּמָה מַאי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the first half of step 24 and asks what case the second half covers.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which practical case of תרומה is governed by רבי יוסי's twilight according to רבי יוחנן?

steps.title: If it means immersion, that time is still a doubt
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the תרומה ruling is about טבילה, then challenges it: during רבי יהודה's twilight it is a doubt, so why be lenient?
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it refers to immersion, isn't that time a doubt?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests one answer: maybe the ruling is about when a כהן may immerse. It immediately attacks this option.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה's twilight is a doubt about whether it is day or night. With שבת we were strict about this doubt. So why would רבי יוחנן be lenient about the same doubt when it comes to טבילה, treating it as daytime by following רבי יוסי?

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (introduces a suggestion that will be challenged)

phrases.english: If you say it refers to immersion — it is a case of uncertainty!
phrases.notes: During רבי יהודה's twilight, it is unclear whether it is day or night, so why be lenient?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proposes one answer to step 25's question and challenges it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that רבי יוחנן's תרומה ruling refers to immersion
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהודה's twilight is a doubt. We were strict about it for שבת, so we should be strict about it for immersion too, and not lenient by following רבי יוסי.
